title: WPMS/3401/2016 of Bhagwati Prasad Ghildiyal AND ANOTHER Vs Zila Sahkari Bank Ltd. AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 3401 of 2016
Bhagwati Prasad Ghildiyal & another ÖÖ.Petitioners
 Versus
Zila Sahkari Bank Ltd. & another ÖRespondents
Mr. P.C. Bisht, Advocate for the petitioners.
Ms. Seema Sah, Advocate for the respondents.
Dated: 05.01.2017
Honíble V.K. Bist, J.

Petitioners have approached this Court
seeking the following reliefs:
ìi). Issue a writ order or direction in the
nature of certiorari for quashing the
impugned notice under Section 13(2) of
the Securitisation and Reconstruction of
Financial Assets and Enforcement of
Security Interest Act, 2002 dated
4.5.2016 sent by the respondents to the
petitioners being arbitrary and illegal
(contained in Annexure No. 1 to the writ
petition) and not to proceed in
furtherance thereof in the meantime.
ii). Issue a writ order or direction in the
nature of mandamus commanding the
respondents to activate the loan account
of the petitioners so that they may
regularly deposit the loan amount in their
account.î
2. Brief facts of the case, as narrated in the writ
petition, are that the petitioners, who are father and son,
were approved a loan of Rs. 15 Lacs on 20.03.2014 by
the Zila Sahkari Bank, Kotdwar, to be paid by Srinagar
Branch of Zila Sahkari Bank with interest @ 10.75%.
The said loan had to be repaid in 15 years in monthly
installment of Rs. 17,500/-. As per the letter dated
20.03.2014, the loan amount had to be repaid in a period
of 15 years and it also reflected that if even after expiry of
15 years the loan remained unpaid, the same could be
recovered with interest. The said loan was taken by the

2
petitioners for building construction and the construction
of the building has been carried out in accordance to the
sanctioned map and, during construction, the Branch
Manager and other employees of the bank made surprise
spot inspection; but, no anomaly was ever found by them.
As per the approval letter dated 20.03.2014 of the
respondents, the loan had to be repaid after the expiry of
one year or after one month from the payment of the last
installment by the bank and this period is called ìgrace
periodî as per the above letter. It is abundantly clear that
the repayment of the loan had to take place after expiry
of one year and for the convenience at the rate of
Rs. 17,500/- per month installment. The payment of the
loan was made to the petitioners by the respondents on
06.06.2014, therefore, the repayment of the loan had to
take place from June, 2015 as per condition 18 of the
approval letter dated 20.03.2014. It is alleged that the
petitioners had made payment of Rs. 1,97,000/- till
31.03.2016 at the rate of per month installment of Rs.
17,500/-. Therefore, till March, 2016 all the installments
as per agreement were repaid. Thereafter, the petitioner
no. 1 fell ill, as he is an old man of about 70 years and he
suffered heart ailment for which he underwent bypass
surgery and studs are fixed in his heart and regularly
thereafter the petitioner no. 1 is getting treatment from
Himalayan Hospital Jolly Grant, Dehradun and he has to
take medicine lifelong. Due to financial crunch, the
repayment in prescribed installments became irregular
for quite sometime. According to the petitioners, the
respondent bank issued impugned notice dated
04.05.2016 under Section 13(2) of the Securitisation and
Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of

3
Security Interest Act, 2002 to the petitioners. Hence, this
writ petition.

3. It is the contention of the learned counsel for
the petitioners that petitioners were regularly paying
installments in time, but, due to the reason that
petitioner no. 1 suffered a massive heart attack and
underwent bypass surgery, they could not deposit few
installments. After recovering from the ailment, the
petitioners, in fact, wanted to deposit the installments
with interest; but, bank did not permit the petitioners to
do the same and issued notice under Section 13(2) of the
Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets
and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioners further
submits that petitioners are ready to pay the entire
outstanding installment alongwith interest within a
period of two weeks and he also undertakes that they will
regularly pay the future installments of the loan.
5. Ms. Seema Sah, learned counsel for the
respondents, on instructions, submits that in case
petitioner pays the entire outstanding installments,
which are due till 31.01.2017 with interest as well as
penal interest before 31.01.2017, the respondent-bank
will certainly consider their request for future installment.
6. In view of the submissions made by the
learned counsel for the parties and in the interest of
justice, the writ petition is disposed of in following
manner:

4
(i) It is directed that the respondent-bank
will give the statement of account to the
petitioners within a period of 10 days from
today.
(ii) In that statement, the respondent-bank
will clarify the outstanding dues, which the
petitioners are liable to pay till 31.01.2017.
(iii) Respondent-bank will also include the
interest as well as the penal interest, if
applicable.
(iv) Thereafter, petitioners will make deposit
the said amount in the bank on or before
31.01.2017.
 (v) In case the said amount is paid by the
petitioners within the stipulated period, the
impugned notice dated 04.05.2016 shall stand
quashed.
(vi) Thereafter, the respondent-bank will
accept the future installment, as fixed by the
bank for remaining period.
7. In case of any default, this order shall stand
recalled automatically and the respondent will be at
liberty to recover the entire remaining amount from the
petitioners.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
 05.01.2017
Navin
